mainTopic: Unwalled settlements, the special redemption rights of לוים and their cities, and whether לוים can own walled-city houses
overview: The משנה teaches that a tiny place, with just two courtyards of two houses each, counts as unwalled even if it has a wall from יהושע's time. The גמרא learns this from extra words in the פסוק and explains why there must be two houses in each courtyard. A new משנה discusses a grandson who inherits a house from his mother's father when one is a לוי and the other a ישראל. רבי holds that the special לוי redemption rule needs both a לוי seller and עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם, while חכמים require only the location. Next, the משנה forbids changing the field, open land and city zones of Levite cities, and the גמרא finds the source in the words 'לֹא יִמָּכֵר'. A ברייתא then shows three things that 'גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם' teaches for a לוי. When the גמרא asks how לוים could own houses in walled cities, רב כהנא's answer is rejected, and a new answer begins that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What counts as houses of the courtyards
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a place with just two courtyards, each with two houses, is treated as unwalled even if it has an old wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the 'houses of the courtyards': two courtyards, each with two houses. Even if the place has a wall from the days of יהושע בן נון, they count as houses of the courtyards.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה defines a tiny settlement. Even if it has a wall, it is treated like an unwalled village.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a wall from יהושע's time gives a house the rules of a walled city (בתי ערי חומה). The משנה says that when the place is this small, the wall doesn't matter. Its houses get the rules of בתי החצרים instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Houses in unwalled settlements, which are treated like fields for redemption
Surrounded by a wall
From the time the Land was conquered, which is the time that sets a city's status as walled

steps.whyThisMatters: A house in a walled city can only be redeemed within a year of the sale. A house in בתי החצרים follows the rules of a field. So this definition decides which set of rules applies.

phrases.english: MISHNA: And these are the houses of the courtyards
phrases.notes: This is the phrase from ויקרא 25:31 for unwalled villages.

phrases.english: two courtyards, each with two houses,
even though it is surrounded by a wall
from the days of Joshua son of Nun,
they are like houses of the courtyards.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the section by defining a term used in the previous משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two courtyards with two houses each count as unwalled, even if they have a wall from יהושע's time.

steps.title: The verse teaches that some walled places count as unwalled
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא points out that the words 'which have no wall' seem extra. It learns from them that some walled places are treated as unwalled.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: once the פסוק says 'houses of the courtyards', don't I already know they have no wall? So why does the פסוק add 'which have no wall'? To teach that even if they have a wall, they are treated as if they have none.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the משנה. It reads extra words in the פסוק as a hint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'houses of the courtyards' already means unwalled villages. So 'which have no wall' looks repeated. The ברייתא says it teaches a new idea: a place can have a real wall and still be judged as unwalled.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
From the plain meaning or implication
Why does the verse need to say this? It points to an extra word that comes to teach something

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
From the meaning of what is said, 'houses of the courtyards',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:31

phrases.english: don't I know that they have no wall?

phrases.aramaic: מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אֲשֶׁר אֵין לָהֶם חוֹמָה״?
phrases.english: Why does the verse say 'which have no wall'?

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם חוֹמָה
phrases.english: Even though they have a wall,
they are like ones that have no wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אֲשֶׁר אֵין לָהֶם חוֹמָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source in the פסוק for the משנה's rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra words 'which have no wall' teach that certain walled places are treated as unwalled.

steps.title: How small the place must be
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא sets the size: houses means at least two, and courtyards means at least two. So it is two courtyards with two houses each.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how many? 'Houses' means two, and 'courtyards' means two. So it is two courtyards, each with two houses.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks which walled places count as unwalled. It answers from the plural words in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plural word means at least two. 'Houses' is plural and 'courtyards' is plural. So the smallest place the פסוק describes is two courtyards with two houses in each. This matches the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: And how many? Asks for the exact size
Courtyards, each shared by houses that open into it

phrases.english: And how many? Houses: two,
courtyards: two,
two courtyards, each with two houses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the exact size of the place described in Step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two courtyards, each with two houses.

steps.title: Maybe it means one house per courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading: maybe 'houses of the courtyards' means just one house in each courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it means a house and a courtyard!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the count of two houses per courtyard. It suggests that one house per courtyard is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק only means one house in each courtyard, the definition changes. Then a walled place with two houses in each courtyard would be too big to count as unwalled. That would go against the משנה's case.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead... It offers another way to read the words
One house and one courtyard

phrases.english: But say it means a house and a courtyard!
phrases.notes: He means one house in each courtyard, not two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in Step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that there must be two houses in each courtyard
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words 'houses of the courtyards' could just mean one house for each courtyard.

steps.title: Then the Torah should have written just courtyards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: if it meant one house per courtyard, the Torah would only need to write 'courtyards'. Writing 'houses' must add something.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the Torah write just 'courtyards'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. If the Torah meant only one house per courtyard, it would not need the word 'houses'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A courtyard always has at least one house. So 'courtyards' alone would already mean one house each. Since the Torah added 'houses', the word must teach that each courtyard has two houses.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let the Torah write (literally: let the Merciful One write)

phrases.english: If so, let the Merciful One write 'courtyards',

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra word 'houses' must teach something
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Houses of the courtyards means one house per courtyard.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'houses' is extra, so it adds a second house to each courtyard.

steps.title: Maybe 'courtyards' alone would mean empty courtyards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a possible problem with its own answer: maybe the word 'houses' is needed, because 'courtyards' alone could mean courtyards with no house.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: if the Torah had written only 'courtyards', it would mean a courtyard without a house...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the word 'houses' is really extra. This sets up the final answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the word 'houses' is there only to show that the courtyards have houses at all. If so, it would not teach that there are two houses per courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say... It brings up a possible objection
A courtyard without a house
Would mean, would imply

phrases.english: And if you say: if the Merciful One had written 'courtyards',
it would mean a courtyard without a house,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the word 'houses' is extra
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Maybe the word 'houses' is needed just to show that the courtyards are lived in.

steps.title: A courtyard without a house is called an enclosure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that an empty walled area is called a קרפף, not a courtyard. So 'courtyards' alone would already mean houses are there.
steps.simpleTranslation: That kind of place is called an enclosure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection. It ends the discussion and confirms the rule of two houses per courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word חצר is only used for an area that has a house. An area with no house is called a קרפף. So 'courtyards' alone would already mean at least one house each. The word 'houses' is extra and teaches two houses per courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: An enclosure, a fenced area with no house
Is called

steps.whatToRemember: Houses of the courtyards means at least two courtyards with two houses each. A place that small counts as unwalled even if it has an ancient wall.

phrases.english: That is called an enclosure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in Step 6 and holds on to the answer in Step 5
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Courtyards' alone might mean an empty courtyard.
steps.terutzMaskana: An empty area is a קרפף, so 'courtyards' alone would already include a house, and 'houses' teaches two.

steps.title: Inheriting a house from a mother's father of a different tribe
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a ישראל who inherits from his mother's father, a לוי, does not redeem the usual way. The same is true of a לוי who inherits from his mother's father, a ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ישראל who inherited from his mother's father, a לוי, does not redeem in this order. And likewise a לוי who inherited from his mother's father, a ישראל, does not redeem in this order.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It deals with a house that passes through the mother's side between a לוי and a ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual order for redeeming houses was taught in the earlier משניות. Here the inheritor and the original owner come from different groups, and the משנה says the usual order does not apply. It does not yet explain why; the גמרא will discuss it.

keyTerms.meaning: His mother's father
Redeems, buys back a sold property
In this order, following the procedure taught before
A member of the tribe of לוי, who has special rules for redeeming houses

steps.confusionAlert: On a first reading, the משנה seems to say the grandson does not use the regular procedure. The גמרא (step 12) rereads it as 'he redeems only by the regular procedure,' because under רבי the לוי rule needs an actual לוי.

phrases.english: MISHNA: An Israelite who inherited
from his mother's father, a Levite,
does not redeem according to this order.
phrases.notes: 'This order' means the redemption rules from the earlier משניות.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן לֵוִי שֶׁיָּרַשׁ אֶת אֲבִי אִמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל —
phrases.english: And likewise, a Levite who inherited from his mother's father, an Israelite,
does not redeem according to this order.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: inheritance between a לוי and a ישראל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the house passes through the mother's side between a לוי and a ישראל, the usual redemption order is not followed.

steps.title: The verse behind the rule and רבי's two requirements
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings the פסוק 'כי בתי ערי הלוים' and states רבי's view: the special rules apply only when there is both a לוי and עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the פסוק says, 'For the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession.' The rule applies only when it is a לוי and the cities of the Levites. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה from the last step continues. It now gives its source from the Torah and says that this is the view of רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The special right to always redeem a house needs two things: the seller must be a לוי, and the house must be in עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם. This explains why the grandson in the משנה, who has only one of these two things, does not get the לוי rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The cities given to the לויים (Levites)
Their permanent possession
A member of the tribe of לוי
Unless there is; only when there is

phrases.english: As it is stated: "For the houses of the cities of the Levites
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:33

phrases.english: are their possession"
[the rule applies only] when there is a Levite and cities of the Levites
These are the words of Rabbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי בָתֵּי עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם הִוא אֲחוּזָּתָם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה begun in step 8 by giving its source and naming whose view it is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, the לוי redemption rules apply only when the seller is a לוי and the house is in עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם.

steps.title: The Sages say the location alone is enough
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree with רבי. The rules depend only on the house being in עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages say: These rules were said only about the cities of the Levites.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings the other side of the מחלוקת. חכמים look only at where the house is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חכמים, it does not matter who the seller is. If the house is in עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם, the special redemption rules apply. This holds even if the owner is not a לוי. So, according to חכמים, the ישראל grandson who inherited a house in עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם would get the special rule.

keyTerms.meaning: These matters were not said (they apply only to...)
Except; only
A disagreement between sages

steps.whatToRemember: רבי requires two things: a לוי seller and עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם. חכמים require only one thing: עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
These matters were not stated
except with regard to the cities of the Levites.
phrases.notes: In other words, the location is what counts, even if the owner is not a לוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין דְּבָרִים הַלָּלוּ אֲמוּרִים אֶלָּא בְּעָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי's view in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to חכמים, the special rules depend only on the house being in עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם.

steps.title: If not the usual way, then like a Levite? But רבי requires a real Levite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the grandson does not redeem the usual way, he must redeem like a לוי. But רבי himself says that only works for an actual לוי in עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, like whom does he redeem? Like a Levite. But then he goes on to teach: 'only when there is a Levite and cities of the Levites'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It points out a contradiction inside רבי's words in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the grandson 'does not redeem in this way,' meaning the usual way for a walled city. The only other option is to redeem like a לוי. But רבי then says the לוי rule needs an actual לוי, and this grandson is a ישראל. So the two parts of the משנה seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Like whom?
A Levite
And then he goes on to teach

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rather, like whom [does he redeem]? Like a Levite.
But then he teaches:
"Only when there is a Levite and cities of the Levites"!
phrases.notes: This is quoting the end of the משנה from step 9. The grandson is not a לוי, so how can he redeem like one?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא כְּמַאן? כְּבֶן לֵוִי. וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first part of the משנה (step 8) using the end of the משנה (step 9).
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the grandson 'does not redeem in this way'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he does not redeem like a ישראל, he must redeem like a לוי. But רבי requires an actual לוי, so the משנה contradicts itself.

steps.title: Read the משנה as: he redeems only the usual way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the משנה. The grandson redeems only the usual way, because the לוי rule needs both a לוי and עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it like this: he redeems only in this usual way, unless there is a Levite and cities of the Levites. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the contradiction by explaining the משנה's words differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of 'he does not redeem the usual way,' read it as 'he redeems only the usual way.' The usual way means the walled-city rule, which gives one year to redeem. This now fits רבי's ending perfectly. The grandson is not a לוי, so he gets only the regular rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Say; read it this way
Redeems; buys back
In this order; the regular procedure

steps.confusionAlert: The new reading flips the meaning. Before, it was 'he does NOT redeem the usual way,' which seemed to mean he redeems like a לוי. Now it is 'he redeems ONLY the usual way,' so according to רבי he does not get the לוי right of always redeeming.

phrases.english: Say:
he redeems only in this procedure,
phrases.notes: This means the regular walled-city rule from the earlier משניות: one year to redeem, then the house stays with the buyer.

phrases.english: unless there is a Levite and cities of the Levites,
These are the words of Rabbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: אֵינוֹ גּוֹאֵל אֶלָּא כַּסֵּדֶר הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say the grandson does not redeem the usual way, which would mean he redeems like a לוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means he redeems only the usual way, since the לוי rule needs both a לוי and עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the seller must be a Levite?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that the cities part comes from the פסוק. It asks for the source that the seller must be a לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that it must be the cities of the Levites, because it is written, 'For the houses of the cities of the Levites.' But from where do we know it must be a Levite?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts one half of רבי's rule and asks for the source of the other half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק quoted in the משנה clearly mentions עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם, so the location requirement is clear. But nothing in those words says the seller himself must be a לוי. The גמרא wants a source for that.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense; granted
As it is written
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: Granted, the cities of the Levites —
as it is written: "For the houses of the cities of the Levites";
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:33

phrases.english: but [that it must be] a Levite, from where do we derive it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם דִּכְתִיב ״כִּי בָּתֵּי עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם״ אֶלָּא לֵוִי מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having settled what רבי means, the גמרא now looks for the source of his second requirement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A Torah source showing that the seller must be a לוי.

steps.title: The source: 'from the Levites'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the start of the same פסוק, which says 'from the Levites.' This shows the house must be bought from a לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And if a man buys from the Levites.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting another part of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מִן הַלְוִיִּם' show that the פסוק is talking about a house sold by a לוי. So רבי's second requirement, that the seller be a לוי, comes straight from the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Here read as 'will buy' (literally 'will redeem')
From the Levites

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי, both requirements come from ויקרא 25:33. 'מִן הַלְוִיִּם' means the seller must be a לוי. 'בָּתֵּי עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם' means the house must be in a לוי city.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And if a man purchases from the Levites."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:33, the beginning of the same פסוק. 'From the Levites' tells us the seller is a לוי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'מִן הַלְוִיִּם' in ויקרא 25:33 show that the seller must be a לוי.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows a לוי redeems at any time even from another לוי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'וַאֲשֶׁר יִגְאַל מִן הַלְוִיִּם'. It teaches that a לוי's right to redeem at any time applies even when the buyer was another לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches about 'And if one redeems from the Levites.' You might think a לוי can redeem at any time from a regular ישראל, because the לוי has the stronger power and the ישראל has the weaker one. Then you might think he cannot do so from another לוי, because both have equally strong power. So the פסוק says 'from the Levites,' to teach that he can redeem at any time even from a לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that uses the same words 'מִן הַלְוִיִּם' from step 14. It shows a לוי can redeem at any time even when he sold to another לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought the power to redeem at any time only works against a weaker buyer, a ישראל, who normally gets only one year. Against another לוי, both sides have the same strong power, so it might cancel out. The words 'מִן הַלְוִיִּם' tell us the seller's power still wins, even when the buyer is a לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might have thought' — opens a wrong idea that the פסוק will correct
His power is made stronger
His power is made weaker
'So the פסוק teaches' — introduces the words that settle the question

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא: 'And if one redeems from the Levites'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:33. The word יִגְאַל literally means 'redeems', and the ברייתא reads it that way.

phrases.english: You might think a Levite may redeem from an Israelite,
because this one's power is made stronger
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the לוי, who can redeem at any time.

phrases.english: and that one's power is made weaker,
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the ישראל, who normally gets only one year to redeem.

phrases.english: but a Levite may not redeem from a Levite,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁזֶּה יִפָּה כֹּחוֹ וְזֶה יִפָּה כֹּחוֹ —
phrases.english: because this one's power is stronger and that one's power is also stronger —
so the verse teaches: 'from the Levites.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and expands the use of 'מִן הַלְוִיִּם' brought in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That the words 'מִן הַלְוִיִּם' teach a rule about a לוי's power to redeem

steps.title: A לוי who is a ממזר or נתין does not get the redemption power
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: 'מִן הַלְוִיִּם' means only some Levites, so a לוי who is a ממזר or נתין is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'From the Levites' means not all Levites. This leaves out a לוי's son who is a ממזר or a נתין.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא learns a second lesson from the word 'מִן', which means 'from' or 'some of'. Not every לוי by birth gets the special power to redeem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מִן' signals a limit. A son of a לוי who is a ממזר or a נתין is still a לוי by his father. But he does not redeem the way a לוי does.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaving out; except for
A child born from a forbidden relationship
A descendant of the גבעונים, who may not marry into the Jewish community

phrases.english: 'From the Levites' — but not all the Levites,
leaving out a Levite's son who is a mamzer or a Gibeonite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second lesson from the same words in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A לוי who is a ממזר or נתין does not have the לוי power to redeem at any time.

steps.title: חכמים do not require the seller to be a לוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains חכמים's view. Only the location in עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם matters, and the seller does not need to be a לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים say: these rules apply only in the cities of the Levites. But we do not say the seller must be a לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the words of חכמים in the משנה. It spells out how they differ from רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, two things are needed: a לוי, and a house in עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם. חכמים need only the location. So even a non-לוי who owns a house there, such as through inheritance, redeems like a לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: These rules are said only about...
We do not say

steps.whatToRemember: רבי needs both a לוי seller and עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם. חכמים need only עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
These matters are not stated
except in the cities of the Levites.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא לֵוִי — לָא אָמְרִינַן.
phrases.english: But 'only if he is a Levite' — we do not say.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין דְּבָרִים הַלָּלוּ אֲמוּרִים אֶלָּא בְּעָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the section by setting חכמים against רבי's two requirements.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to חכמים, the special redemption rule depends only on the house being in עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם, not on the seller being a לוי.

steps.title: The land areas of the Levite cities may not be switched
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a field, the open land, and the city area around עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם may not be turned into one another.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not make a field into open land, or open land into a field. We do not make open land into city, or city into open land.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets a rule that each zone of a Levite city must stay what it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Levite cities had set zones: the city itself, the open land around it, and fields beyond that. The משנה forbids changing any zone into a neighboring one, in either direction.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Open land around a Levite city, kept empty
A field for planting
We do not make; it is not allowed to turn into

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may not make a field into open land,
phrases.notes: מִגְרָשׁ is the empty strip of land kept around a Levite city.

phrases.english: nor open land into a field,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא מִגְרָשׁ עִיר, וְלֹא עִיר מִגְרָשׁ.
phrases.english: nor open land into city, nor city into open land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic about the Levite cities.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The field, open-land, and city zones of עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם may not be changed into one another.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר limits the rule to Levite cities
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the ban on changing land use applies only in עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם. In Israelite cities some one-way changes are allowed so the cities are not ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: When does this rule apply? In the cities of the Levites. But in Israelite cities you may turn a field into open land, but not open land into a field. You may turn open land into city, but not city into open land, so that the cities of Israel will not be ruined.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the משנה, רבי אלעזר limits the rule from step 18 so that it covers only the cities of the לוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 said you may never switch field, open land, and city in עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם. רבי אלעזר agrees about Levite cities, but says that in Israelite cities the change may go in only one direction. The reason he gives is to keep Israelite cities from being destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said? This phrase limits a rule to certain cases.
The open land around a city, with no houses and no planted fields
Ordinary cities of Israelites, not the cities given to the לוים
So that they will not ruin or destroy

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר does not disagree about Levite cities. He only adds a separate rule for Israelite cities.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים?
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: "These words" is the rule from the line before: you may not switch field, open land, and city.

phrases.english: In the cities of the Levites,
but in the cities of Israelites

phrases.aramaic: עוֹשִׂין שָׂדֶה מִגְרָשׁ, וְלֹא מִגְרָשׁ שָׂדֶה,
phrases.english: one may make a field into open land, but not open land into a field;
open land into city, but not city into open land,
so that they will not ruin the cities of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of step 18 to Levite cities and adds a rule for Israelite cities
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In Israelite cities: field may become open land, and open land may become city, but not the reverse

steps.title: Priests and Levites may sell and redeem at any time
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that כהנים and לוים may sell their land at any time and redeem it at any time, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The priests and the Levites may sell at any time and redeem at any time, as it says: 'The Levites shall have a redemption forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new rule: כהנים and לוים have a lasting right to sell and to buy back their property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is the words 'גְּאוּלַּת עוֹלָם', a redemption 'forever.' This means the right to redeem never runs out. כהנים are included because they are also from the tribe of לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: They may sell at any time
They redeem, meaning they buy the property back
A redemption forever, a right to redeem that never ends

phrases.english: The priests and the Levites may sell at any time,
and they may redeem at any time,
as it says: "The Levites shall have a redemption forever."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:32

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New rule in the משנה about selling and redeeming
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים and לוים may sell and redeem at any time

steps.title: Where do we learn that Levite land may not be changed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אלעזר and points out that everyone agrees Levite cities may not be changed. It asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: 'When does this rule apply? In the cities of the Levites, but in the cities of Israelites one may...' and so on. In any case, everyone agrees that in the Levite cities we do not change anything. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It quotes the משנה and asks where the agreed rule about Levite cities comes from, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר and the earlier תנא differ only about Israelite cities. Both agree that in עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם nothing may be changed. Since this is accepted by all, the גמרא wants its source in the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone, meaning all the opinions agree
We change something from its current use
From where do we know these things? A request for a source
And so on. The quote continues, but the rest is not written out.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Elazar said:
"In what case are these words said? In the cities of the Levites,
but in the cities of Israelites one may make…" and so on.
In any case, according to everyone,
phrases.notes: "Everyone" means both רבי אלעזר and the first opinion in the משנה.

phrases.english: in the cities of the Levites we do not change anything,
from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי אלעזר's ruling and asks for the source of the part everyone agrees on
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for the rule that Levite land may not be changed

steps.title: The source: 'it shall not be sold'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר brings the פסוק 'וּשְׂדֵה מִגְרַשׁ עָרֵיהֶם לֹא יִמָּכֵר' as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Because the verse says: 'But the field of the open land of their cities shall not be sold.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question with a פסוק about the open land around Levite cities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about the open land of Levite cities, so it fits the topic. What exactly 'לֹא יִמָּכֵר' means is not clear yet, and the next steps work this out.

keyTerms.meaning: Because the verse says
It shall not be sold

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: Because the verse says:
"But the field of the open land of their cities shall not be sold."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:34

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'וּשְׂדֵה מִגְרַשׁ עָרֵיהֶם לֹא יִמָּכֵר'

steps.title: It cannot mean 'never sold at all'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'לֹא יִמָּכֵר' means. It cannot mean no sale at all, because 'גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם' shows that לוים do sell.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'shall not be sold' mean? If you say it may not be sold at all, that is hard to accept. Since it is written 'The Levites shall have a redemption forever,' we can see that they do sell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the simple reading of the פסוק and shows it cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can only redeem something you already sold. Since the Torah gives לוים a right to redeem forever, they must be allowed to sell. So 'לֹא יִמָּכֵר' cannot mean that selling is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. This brings up a possible reading so it can be tested.
By implication, something we can learn from what was said
That they do sell

phrases.english: What does "shall not be sold" mean?
If you say it may not be sold at all,
but from the fact that it is written:
"The Levites shall have a redemption forever,"
we can see that they do sell.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״לֹא יִמָּכֵר״? אִילֵּימָא לֹא יִמָּכֵר כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the simple reading of the פסוק brought in step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'לֹא יִמָּכֵר' as a complete ban on selling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם' assumes that a sale took place, so selling cannot be forbidden

steps.title: 'Not sold' means 'not changed'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'לֹא יִמָּכֵר' means the land's use may not be changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'shall not be sold' mean? It shall not be changed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct reading of the פסוק, which answers the question from step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since selling is allowed, 'not sold' must mean something else: the land may not be moved into a different category. This is the source that a field, open land, and city in עָרֵי הַלְוִיִּם must stay as they are.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall not change it, meaning its use or category stays the same

steps.whatToRemember: The words 'לֹא יִמָּכֵר' in the פסוק teach 'לֹא יְשַׁנֶּה': in Levite cities, field, open land, and city may not be turned into one another.

phrases.english: Rather, what does "shall not be sold" mean?
It shall not be changed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 by reading the פסוק a new way
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לֹא יִמָּכֵר' means no sale at all
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לֹא יִמָּכֵר' means the land's category may not be changed

steps.title: Why does the Torah need 'redemption forever'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule. A ברייתא asks what the words 'גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם' come to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: The priests and the Levites may sell at any time and redeem at any time. The Rabbis taught: 'The Levites shall have a redemption forever.' Why does the verse need to say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא that asks why the פסוק is needed. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumes every word of the Torah teaches something. It asks what new point the phrase 'גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם' adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the verse need to say this? What does it come to teach?

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּהֲנִים וְהַלְוִיִּם מוֹכְרִין לְעוֹלָם וְגוֹאֲלִין לְעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: The priests and the Levites may sell at any time and redeem at any time.
The Rabbis taught:
"The Levites shall have a redemption forever,"
why does the verse need to say this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next rule in the משנה (step 20)
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the words 'גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם' come to teach

steps.title: A Levite does not have to wait to redeem
steps.stepSummary: An Israelite must wait 'a number of years of crops' before redeeming. We might think a לוי must wait too, so the Torah says 'גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם' to teach that he may redeem at any time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it says: 'According to the number of years of crops he shall sell to you,' you might think this is true here too. So the verse says: 'The Levites shall have a redemption forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The פסוק is needed so that we do not apply the Israelite waiting time to a לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An Israelite who sells his field must wait some years of crops before he may redeem it. Without a special פסוק, we would apply the same wait to a לוי. 'גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם' teaches that a לוי may redeem at any time, even right after the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought. This brings up a mistaken idea that the פסוק then rules out.
Years of crops, the time a buyer gets to use the field before it can be redeemed
Therefore the verse says. This brings the פסוק that settles the point.

steps.whatToRemember: An Israelite must wait before redeeming his field, but a לוי may redeem right away, because of 'גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם'.

phrases.english: Since it says:
"According to the number of years of crops he shall sell to you,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:15. This is about an Israelite's field, which he must wait to redeem.

phrases.english: you might think this one is the same?
phrases.notes: "This one" is the לוי who sold his land.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says: "The Levites shall have a redemption forever."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק teaches that a לוי, unlike an Israelite, may redeem right away without waiting years of crops

steps.title: A Levite's consecrated field does not go to the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives a second lesson from 'גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם'. A field that was consecrated and not redeemed normally goes to the כהנים in the יובל. A לוי's field does not, because he can always redeem it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Torah says a consecrated field becomes 'holy to ה׳' when it goes out in the יובל, we might think the same is true for a לוי's field. So the Torah says 'The Levites shall have a perpetual redemption.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its answer from the last step. It shows a second rule that 'גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם' tells us does not apply to לוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a regular Israelite, a field consecrated to the בית המקדש and not redeemed before the יובל goes to the כהנים for good. One could think a לוי's field follows that rule too. 'גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם' teaches that a לוי's field never leaves him this way, because he can always redeem it.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it is said: introduces a פסוק that might lead us to a wrong idea
One might think: introduces a possible mistaken idea
The verse teaches: introduces the פסוק that corrects the mistake
The Jubilee year, every fiftieth year, when land returns
Holy to ה׳: here it means the field goes to the כהנים

phrases.english: Since it is stated:
"And the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee,
shall be holy to the Lord,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:21

phrases.english: one might think that this too is so?
phrases.notes: 'This' means a field that a לוי consecrated.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse teaches:
"The Levites shall have a perpetual redemption."

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיֹּבֵל קֹדֶשׁ לַה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second lesson from the same words 'גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What 'גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם' comes to teach (from step 25).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A לוי's consecrated field is not passed to the כהנים in the יובל; he can always redeem it.

steps.title: A Levite's house in a walled city is not lost forever
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives a third lesson. A house in a walled city that is not redeemed within a year belongs to the buyer forever. A לוי's house does not, because he can always redeem it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Torah says a house in a walled city stays with the buyer forever, we might think the same is true for a לוי's house. So the Torah says 'The Levites shall have a perpetual redemption.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its third and last lesson from 'גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם'. This time it is about a house, not a field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if someone sells a house in a walled city and does not buy it back within one year, the buyer keeps it forever, even past the יובל. 'גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם' teaches that a לוי who sells such a house can always buy it back.

keyTerms.term: בַּיִת אֲשֶׁר בָּעִיר אֲשֶׁר לוֹ חוֹמָה
keyTerms.meaning: A house in a walled city, which has its own selling rules
Permanently, forever; the house is never returned

steps.whyThisMatters: This third lesson is the one the גמרא will question in the next step.

phrases.english: Since it is stated:
"Then the house that is in the city
that has a wall shall stand permanently,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:30

phrases.english: one might think that this too is so?
phrases.notes: 'This' means a house that a לוי sold in a walled city.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse teaches:
"The Levites shall have a perpetual redemption."

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְקָם הַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר בָּעִיר אֲשֶׁר לוֹ חוֹמָה לַצְּמִיתוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third lesson from 'גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם', now about houses.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What 'גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם' comes to teach (from step 25).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A לוי's house in a walled city does not become the buyer's forever; he can always redeem it.

steps.title: Do Levites even have houses in walled cities?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the first two lessons about fields. It challenges the third, because another ברייתא says the cities of the לוים were medium-sized towns, not large walled cities.
steps.simpleTranslation: The two lessons about fields are fine. But do לוים have houses in walled cities? A ברייתא says their cities were not small villages and not large walled cities, only medium-sized towns!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the third lesson of the ברייתא. It brings another ברייתא that seems to say לוים never lived in walled cities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lessons about fields make sense. But the house lesson needs לוים to own houses in walled cities. If the cities of the לוים were always medium towns without walls, why would the Torah need to teach a rule for that case?

keyTerms.meaning: Granted: accepts one point before challenging another
It is fine, it works
Small villages
Large walled cities
Medium-sized towns

phrases.english: Granted, these two are fine,
phrases.notes: The two lessons about a לוי's field, from steps 26 and 27.

phrases.english: but houses of walled cities,
do the Levites have them?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
These cities, one does not make them
neither small villages
nor large cities,
but rather medium-sized towns!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא הָנֵי תַּרְתֵּי לְחַיֵּי, אֶלָּא בָּתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה לִלְוִיִּם מִי אִית לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the third lesson (step 28) as describing a case that seems impossible.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's lesson that a לוי's house in a walled city can always be redeemed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא says the cities of the לוים were medium towns, not large walled cities, so the case seems to never happen.

steps.title: רב כהנא: walled first, or settled first
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that the two ברייתות speak about different towns. One speaks of a town walled first and settled later. The other speaks of a town settled first and walled later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: This is not a problem. Here it means a town that was walled and then settled. There it means a town that was settled and then walled.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the challenge. He shows that the two ברייתות are talking about two different kinds of towns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא saying the cities of the לוים were not large walled cities refers to a town that was walled first and settled later. The ברייתא giving the house rule refers to a medium town settled first by the לוים and walled later. So a לוי can own a house in a walled city, and the lesson in step 28 has a real case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult: the two sources speak of different cases
It was surrounded by a wall
It was settled, people lived there
Afterwards, later on

steps.whatToRemember: 'גְּאֻלַּת עוֹלָם' teaches three things for a לוי: he may redeem at any time, his consecrated field does not go to the כהנים, and his house in a walled city is never lost forever. רב כהנא's way of explaining how a לוי could own a walled-city house is challenged right away in steps 31–33, and step 34 begins a different answer.
steps.confusionAlert: The order matters. 'Walled then settled' and 'settled then walled' are not the same, and each ברייתא is talking about a different one.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: It is not difficult.
Here, it is a town that was walled and later settled;
there, it is a town that was settled and later walled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 29 by splitting the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (כאן... כאן...): each source speaks about a different kind of town.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לוים never had houses in walled cities, so the house lesson would have no case.
steps.terutzMaskana: A town settled by לוים and walled later gives them walled-city houses, so the lesson applies.

steps.title: Does a wall built after settling even count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב כהנא. A ברייתא says a city counts as walled only if it was walled first and settled later, not settled first and walled later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a city like this (settled first, walled later) even considered walled? But a ברייתא teaches on the פסוק 'a dwelling house in a walled city': it means a city that was walled first and settled afterward, not one that was settled first and walled afterward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב כהנא's answer from Step 30. It quotes a ברייתא showing that a town settled first and walled later does not count as a walled city at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא needed a לוי town that is also a walled city, so he pointed to a town settled first and walled later. The ברייתא says that kind of town is not an עיר חומה. So רב כהנא's case would not have the walled-city rule, and the third lesson of the ברייתא about a לוי's house is left without a case.

keyTerms.meaning: A walled city. A house sold there can only be redeemed within one year.
It was surrounded by a wall.
It was settled. People came to live in it.
Is it really considered...? This opens a challenging question.

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the order of the words. 'הוקף ולבסוף ישב' means wall first, people later, and that one counts. 'ישב ולבסוף הוקף' means people first, wall later, and that one does not count.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי הַאי גַּוְונָא מִי הָוְיָא חוֹמָה?
phrases.english: And in a case like this, is it considered a wall?
phrases.notes: 'A case like this' is רב כהנא's town, which was settled first and walled later.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְאִישׁ כִּי יִמְכֹּר בֵּית מוֹשַׁב עִיר חוֹמָה״
phrases.english: "And if a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:29

phrases.english: meaning one that was walled and afterward settled,
and not one that was settled and afterward walled.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הַאי גַּוְונָא מִי הָוְיָא חוֹמָה? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer רב כהנא gave in Step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's claim that a town settled first and walled later can be a walled לוי city.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא defines a walled city as one walled before it was settled. A town walled after settling is not an עיר חומה, so רב כהנא's case fails.

steps.title: The wall must be built by גוים
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא continues. A wall built by Jews does not count. Through a matching word 'חומה' in another פסוק, it teaches that the wall must be built by גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think it counts even if Jews put the wall around it. So it says here 'wall', and it says there 'wall'. Just as there it means walls built by גוים, so here it means walls built by גוים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same ברייתא. It adds a second condition: the wall must have been built by גוים, not by Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא links the word 'חומה' in our פסוק to the same word in the פסוק about the cities of עוג. Those walls were built by גוים, so our walled cities must also have walls built by גוים. This makes the definition of an עיר חומה even narrower, which makes it harder to fit a לוי city into it.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought... This brings up a possible mistaken idea so the ברייתא can reject it.
It says here... and it says there. This links two פסוקים through the same word.
Non-Jews.

phrases.english: One might think: even if Jews surrounded it with a wall?
It says here "wall,"
and it says there "wall,"
phrases.notes: 'There' is דברים 3:5, about the walled cities of עוג.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן גּוֹיִם, אַף כָּאן גּוֹיִם.
phrases.english: just as there it means walls built by גוים, so too here, walls built by גוים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא that was quoted as the challenge in Step 31.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the wall has to be built by גוים, then a wall the לוים added later to their own town cannot count.

steps.title: The wall must come before the conquest
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with a third condition. Even a wall built by גוים counts only if it was built before the Jews conquered the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think it counts even if גוים put the wall around it later. So it says there 'wall' and here 'wall'. Just as there the walls were built by גוים before that time, so here, by גוים before that time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא. The wall has to be built by גוים before the conquest of ארץ ישראל. Together, this whole ברייתא is the challenge against רב כהנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the same link to the cities of עוג, the ברייתא adds a time limit. Those walls were already standing when the Jews arrived. So only walls from before the conquest count. A town that the לוים settled and that was walled only later can never qualify. The exclamation at the end shows the challenge is now complete.

keyTerms.meaning: Afterward. Here it means after the Jews conquered the land.
Beforehand. Here it means before the conquest.

steps.whatToRemember: According to this ברייתא, an עיר חומה needs three things: it was walled before it was settled, by גוים, and before the Jews conquered the land. That seems to rule out רב כהנא's town that was settled first and walled later.

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ הִקִּיפוּהָ גּוֹיִם לְאַחַר מִכֵּן?
phrases.english: One might think: even if גוים surrounded it with a wall afterward?
phrases.notes: 'Afterward' means after the Jews conquered the land.

phrases.english: It says there "wall," and it says here "wall,"
just as there it was גוים, before that time,
so too here, גוים before that time!

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ הִקִּיפוּהָ גּוֹיִם לְאַחַר מִכֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברייתא and completes the challenge to רב כהנא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only walls built by גוים before the conquest count. A wall added to a לוי town after it was settled can never make it an עיר חומה.

steps.title: A new answer: walled cities that came to the לוים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בריה דרב סלא חסידא gives a new answer before רב פפא. He begins describing a case where walled cities 'fell to' the לוים. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף, son of רב סלא חסידא, explained it before רב פפא: for example, where they received...
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב כהנא's answer was knocked down, a new sage offers another way to explain the ברייתא. The sentence is cut off here, so the גמרא is setting up an answer that finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a town that was walled later, he points to a city that was already walled by גוים before the conquest and then came to the לוים. A city like that does meet all the conditions of the ברייתא. The rest of his explanation comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it, meaning he gave an interpretation of the ברייתא.
For example, in a case where...
Literally 'they fell to them': the cities came into their share when the land was divided.

phrases.aramaic: תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב סַלָּא חֲסִידָא
phrases.english: Rav Yosef, son of Rav Sala the Pious, explained it
before Rav Pappa:
for example, where they fell to them
phrases.notes: 'Them' is the לוים. The sentence keeps going on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב סַלָּא חֲסִידָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to the original contradiction from Step 29, after רב כהנא's answer was challenged in Steps 31–33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a different case: a walled city that came to the לוים, rather than a town walled after settling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that the לוים' cities could never be walled cities, because a wall added later does not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: A city already walled by גוים before the conquest that came to the לוים would count as a walled city. The details continue in the next section.
